newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND RECORD FIRST VICTORY IN ZIMBABWE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND RECORD FIRST VICTORY IN ZIMBABWE.

text.p: A vastly-improved performance from their bowlers carried England to the first victory of their Zimbabwe tour when they defeated Matabeleland by 59 runs in a one-day match at Bulawayo Athletic Club on Sunday.

Chasing a target of 211, the home side were bowled out for 151, off-spinner Robert Croft undermining the middle order with three for 42. Pacemen Darren Gough and Alan Mullally also produced highly economical spells and shared three wickets.
England's innings was built on opener Nick Knight's 58 but the final total was disappointing as the touring side fell from 116 for two to 210 for nine.

The Whittall cousins, Guy and Andrew, who are both in the Zimbabwe squad for the first one-day international next Sunday, took seven wickets between them as four men were caught on the short leg side boundary.
Captain Mike Atherton ended his run of three single figure scores -- 0, 2 and 7 -- by making a fluent 28 at a run-a-ball, hitting five fours, before turning the ball into the hands of mid-wicket.
Nasser Hussain fell in the same area before Graham Thorpe (11) and John Crawley (30) were both caught at deep square leg.
Jack Russell -- playing ahead of Alec Stewart who was troubled by back spasms -- lifted a full toss into the same area to go for 15 while Ronnie Irani (20) hit a catch to mid-wicket.
After a spate of wides in previous games, England finally found their line and Matabeleland were never up with the asking rate.
Although three batsmen reached 30, none were able to play the lengthy innings needed as England finally produced a disciplined performance in the field.
Gough finished with one for 17 from 8.3 overs and Mullally two for 14 from seven.
England, who lost their previous two tour matches, begin a four-day game against the same opposition on Tuesday.
